Depending on your talents, career ambitions and qualifications, you can choose to study one of four pathways suited to your individual needs. As well as your qualification, your study programme will include career enhancing work placements, exciting enrichment opportunities, impartial careers advice and guidance, as well as access to a range of wellbeing and student support services. A Levels Bury College A Level Centre is a great place to study. We are an inclusive college community that will support you to achieve your full potential through an engaging, interesting and personalised study programme. Click here to visit this page Vocational Programmes Our vocational study programmes use practical and theoretical learning to help you develop work-related skills and technical understanding. The college is committed to providing you with the skills and knowledge needed to progress your career. Click here to visit this page T Levels T Levels are new, high-quality technical qualifications which are an exciting alternative to A-levels and apprenticeships. You will combine classroom theory with practical learning and an 45-day industry placement. Click here to visit this page Apprenticeships An apprenticeship is a job where you will have the opportunity to learn new skills, gain experience and get paid. By the end of an apprenticeship, you will have the right skills and knowledge needed for your chosen career. Apprenticeships - Bury College Skip to main content Skip to search Skip to navigation Open action menu Campus map Contact us Course guides Apply now Apprenticeships What is an Apprenticeship? An Apprenticeship is a paid job where you learn, gain experience and develop skills. As an Apprentice with Bury College you will: Learn and train for a specific job. Get paid and receive holiday leave. Receive hands-on experience in a real job. Spend a minimum of 6 hours a week off-the-job to develop the skills, knowledge and behaviours relevant to your Apprenticeship standard. Complete assessments during, and at the end, of your Apprenticeship. Be on a career path with lots of future potential. COURSE SEARCH Search Apprenticeship courses {{ status }} Please enter your search query above to begin searching courses. {{item.courseTitle}} (Click to view full course details) {{item.areaTypeText}} {{item.typeOfStudyText}} Summary of course: Click to view full course details View all of our Apprenticeship courses here Who can do an apprenticeship? Apprenticeships are available to anyone aged 16 and over. Whether you are a school leaver looking to start your career, or an adult looking to upskill or explore a new career path, an apprenticeship could be a great option for you. How much do apprentices get paid? You will earn a minimum of £8 per hour if you’re either: Aged under 19. Aged 19 or over in the first year of an apprenticeship. You are entitled to the minimum wage for your age if you are aged 19 or over and have completed the first year of your apprenticeship. Click here to go to the Government website for more information. Applying for an apprenticeship Your next step towards securing an apprenticeship depends on your situation. Please use the buttons below for further guidance. Click here if you are still in education Click here if you are looking for an employer Contact us if you are already employed Do you want to employ an apprentice? Bury College specialises in high-quality apprenticeships in a range of industry sectors. Our Apprenticeship Team will work with you to find the programme that fits your business needs, as well as the apprentices’ goals. Click here to contact us Why study an apprenticeship at Bury College? Bury College has a range of apprenticeship programmes aimed at helping you reach your full potential. Our apprenticeships are available in a range of sectors and have been developed by employers to ensure professional training and career progression. As an apprentice, you are part of our Bury College community, and have access to the same support as other students. In addition to your dedicated Learning and Skills Coach, our Student Services team offers a ‘one-stop shop’ with support that extends to all aspects of student life. What level do apprenticeships start at? Apprenticeships start at different levels. The level you start at will depend on your qualifications. Most apprenticeships start at Level 2. To start at Level 3 (A Level equivalent), you will likely need at least one grade 4 GCSE in Maths or English. However, employers will set their own entry requirements for the job role and generally will expect you to have both Maths and English at grade 4. At the end of your apprenticeship, you will achieve the equivalent education level. For example, if you complete a level 3 apprenticeship, you will gain the equivalent of an A level. Level 2 is the equivalent of a GCSE. How are apprenticeships assessed? You will complete assessments during and at the end of your apprenticeship. This could be done in the following ways: Observations Professional/Guided Discussions Questions and Answers Reflective Accounts Work Product Evidence Witness Statements Reviews The End Point Assessment will be conducted by an official Awarding Body to test if you are competent in your occupation. Work For Us | Vacancies - Bury College Skip to main content Skip to search Skip to navigation Open action menu Campus map Contact us Course guides Apply now Work For Us Bury College is an institute of higher learning for ages 16 and above. We pride ourselves on developing skills for life in our learners across our different courses. As a college, we offer A Levels, T Levels, vocational courses, apprenticeships, foundation studies as well as university and adult courses. Aspiring to provide the best for every student lies at the heart of all that we do. In order to help us meet that aspiration, we know our number one asset is our staff. Attracting, developing and retaining excellent people is our primary goal. People who share the College values and support each other to deliver the College’s mission of serving its communities through education and training. Meet some of our staff who share their experiences of what life is like working at Bury College. Rizwan Qureshi - Accounting Lecturer “There is a real sense of community here at Bury College and a feeling that we’re all in this together. I really enjoy my job and the fact that I have the opportunity to support students when they’re at a crossroads in their education and careers.” Mark Fisher - Student Information Senior Officer for Registry “There is always support available should I need help, and the wellbeing of staff is really well looked after across the College.” Other useful pages More information on Do you have the tools to teach Construction at Bury College? We are working with the Department for Education to deliver a new initiative that is offering: A fully funded teaching qualification (PGCE/CertEd) taught over two years which will allow you to teach those aged 14+ A package of intensive support to help you during the first few months as a teacher, including from your line manager, learning improvement leaders and peers A reduced teaching timetable in your first two years In addition to this support package you will be recruited to one of our vacant Trainee Lecturer positions, and on successful completion of the probation period will secure a permanent teaching contract. Ofsted Good Provider - Bury College Skip to main content Skip to search Skip to navigation Open action menu Campus map Contact us Course guides Apply now Ofsted Good Provider Bury College ‘where there is a culture of high expectations and mutual respect’ receives a Good Ofsted rating Staff and students at Bury College are celebrating after once again being recognised as a Good college following a recent Ofsted inspection. The Ofsted report highlights the positive practices which are taking place across the College and recognises that ‘learners behave very well in college and at work’ and also mentions that ‘Bury College has a supportive and inclusive environment.’ Comments from the report include: Bury College has a supportive and inclusive environment, where there is a culture of high expectations and mutual respect. Learners and apprentices behave very well in college and at work. Learners and apprentices develop confidence as a result of their courses. Learners and apprentices appreciate the support and encouragement they receive from staff. The report confirms the good quality of teaching, learning and assessment and praises leaders for establishing appropriate links with a range of stakeholders enabling them to ‘effectively use information about local and regional skills needs and plan courses to meet these needs’. Charlie Deane, Bury College Principal and Chief Executive is delighted: “This is wonderful news for Bury, Bury College and the communities we serve. The report reflects the hard work of our staff, students, governors, parents and partners and supports the Bury College vision of excellent outcomes and positive futures for all.” Becky Tootell, Bury College Deputy Principal – Curriculum and Quality added, “I am delighted for our staff, students and governors. Their commitment and hard work have rightly been recognised by Ofsted as delivering high quality education and training. It is great to see that the behaviour of our students has been praised in the report. Sustainability | About Us - Bury College Skip to main content Skip to search Skip to navigation Open action menu Campus map Contact us Course guides Apply now Sustainability The Green College Commitment Bury College is on the journey to achieving the Green College Commitment and is focused on embedding green and sustainable technologies throughout the curriculum. Good practice in education for sustainability is embraced throughout teaching, learning, and assessment. Annual reduction in CO2 emissions ↓6% Annual decrease in gas use ↓5% Annual decrease in electricity use ↓11% Annual increase in water consumption ↑37% Annual decrease in landfill waste ↓38% Annual number of students engaged in sustainability awareness - 4,178 Bury College proudly marked Green Week 2025 with a series of impactful sustainability initiatives across campus. Over the course of the week: 201 trees and more than 194 flowers—including Maple, Cherry, Birch, Pansies, and more—were planted, helping to save an estimated 5,025 kg of CO₂e annually. 120 new dry mixed recycling bins were introduced, making it easier for everyone to recycle correctly. Separate food waste bins will soon be available in dining areas and staff rooms. 65 students in 6 groups collected an impressive 63 kg of litter from around campus. 43 staff members commuted using green travel options, saving a total of 1,110.8 miles and reducing carbon emissions by 870 kg CO₂e. The College hosted a successful Bike Day with free service and maintenance checks provided by the National Cycling Association (NCA). Bury College also participated in the RSPB’s Big Garden Birdwatch, supporting local biodiversity. Bury College is also proud to have been awarded Approved Travel Plan Modeshift STARS accreditation for efforts to increase levels of walking, cycling and other forms of sustainable travel. Support For Schools | About Us - Bury College Skip to main content Skip to search Skip to navigation Open action menu Campus map Contact us Course guides Apply now Support For Schools Our Student Recruitment Team works closely with schools, education providers, and careers professionals to share valuable information about the wide range of opportunities available at Bury College. Our goal is to raise aspirations and empower pupils with the knowledge and guidance they need to make confident, informed decisions about their future pathways. Find on this page: Support services we offer Frequently asked questions Key dates for your calendar Matrix accreditation Speak to our Student Recruitment team Support services we offer In line with the Gatsby benchmarks, we offer a range of services to help support pupils with their progression to college, helping make sure that they are fully equipped and have all the information they need to make the right choice for their future. Assembly talks We deliver a variety of engaging presentations, including our Aspirational Presentation, Apprenticeships Presentation, and T Level Presentation. These sessions can be delivered as whole-year assemblies or smaller tutorial sessions for Year 10 and 11 pupils across schools in Bury and the surrounding areas. STEM presentation and workshops A 1 hour classroom based session. Learn about the opportunities that studying Science subjects could lead to in the future. Studying Science and Maths will prepare you for a job that will put you in the driving seat, giving you skills and knowledge to improve the world around us, and even the future of the planet. Application support We can visit your school at lunchtime or after school to provide pupils with tailored support throughout the application process. This helps to ensure that the majority of pupils submit their applications ahead of our priority application deadline (for those applying to start in September 2026, our priority application deadline is the 24th November 2025 ). Careers events We can provide support at a wide range of careers events, including Year 9 options events and evenings, careers fairs, and CV writing or transferable skills workshops. Parents evenings We can provide support at Parents' Evenings and Options Evenings, providing pupils with advice and guidance on the opportunities available at Bury College. Frequently asked questions Find out the answers to some of the most frequent questions we receive from high schools. Can I track a pupil's application? Pupil's applications can be tracked through the school’s portal. Log in details are personal to each user; if you do not have a log in set up, or you are struggling to access the system, our Admissions Team can support you with this. Please contact them on 0161 280 8200 or via email at admissions@burycollege.ac.uk . Can pupils apply for more than one course? Yes, pupils can apply for more than one course; many of our A Level students also apply for a Vocational course. It’s always good for students to have options! Do we offer tours of the College? Year 11 students who were unable to attend Open Events, or those with additional needs, are welcome to email schools@burycollege.ac.uk to arrange a personalised tour. Do you hold tours for small groups? We are pleased to offer tours of our facilities for small groups upon request, subject to availability. If we can't book in for an assembly presentation, how can pupils still access information about the courses on offer? If you can't book in for an assembly presentation, we will work with you to ensure the information your pupils need is still provided to support and educate them on their choices at College. Are you able to visit our school? We will do our best to be available to support at your school. We will prioritise Year 11 events, so please send us your dates as early as possible. Once received, we will schedule them in our diary and aim to have a member of our Student Recruitment Team attend. Please can we have some Bury College course guides to hand out to pupils? Yes! By contacting our team, you can arrange a delivery of course guides for Year 10 and 11 pupils. If you have an upcoming event and haven’t yet received course guides, please let us know when booking, and we can bring copies along to the event. When are the Bury College Open Events? Our Open Events will take place on the dates below: Tuesday 7th October 2025 Thursday 16th October 2025 Saturday 8th November 2025 Thursday 26th March 2026 The first 30 minutes of each event has a designated quiet session, providing a more relaxed atmosphere for those who prefer it. Full details, including how to book, can be found on our Events page . Can you support with College applications? We are happy to visit schools to provide advice and support for pupils who are considering applying to the College or have questions about the application process. Sessions can be scheduled during form time, as lunchtime drop-ins, or after school. Please get in touch to arrange a booking.
